clue.text: Trip going to bar is cause of difficulty

parts.note: tripping as you walk along is stumbling
a bar or obstruction is a block

explanation.surface: Someone who trips on the way to the pub blames the obstacle for all their trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle that holds up progress is the idiom's meaning: a hindrance in the path of any plan.

clue.text: Cocktail, one for the road?

explanation.surface: A drink offered before setting off on the drive home.
explanation.definitionFit: A brandy and orange-liqueur cocktail shares its name with the passenger car bolted to a motorbike for travel.

clue.text: Churlish about losing on Alps ski-run, met trouble

indicators.note: trouble means the preceding letters are stirred up into disorder

explanation.surface: A skier on an Alpine run hits trouble and sulks about losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ON ALPS SKI-RUN MET; 'about losing' belongs to the definition, describing a bad loser.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad loser behaves ungraciously, failing to show sporting fairness in defeat.

clue.text: Fight, yet about nothing!

indicators.note: about means the word for yet is wrapped around the zero for nothing; that the solution's letters also run on inside this word is a coincidence

parts.note: yet and but are synonyms as conjunctions
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A protest that a brawl was really over nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a boxing contest or round of fighting, a synonym.

clue.text: Take cover!

parts.note: an order to buy an insurance policy, not to duck for shelter

explanation.surface: A shouted warning to duck for shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange a policy against loss is to get protection from an insurer.

clue.text: Benefit announced, then denied

parts.note: a benefit is a gain
announced means said

explanation.surface: A welfare payment is declared and then withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or refuse to accept, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Standard-bearing, like a good citizen?

parts.note: a law is a standard or rule
bearing in the sense of enduring or putting up with is abiding

explanation.surface: Carrying the flag, like a model member of society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard-bearing' suggests a flag carrier; split it as standard (law) plus bearing (abiding, tolerating).
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen who obeys every rule keeps faith with the legal code.

clue.text: Latin-derived name for a rose, would you say?

definitions.text: Latin-derived name for a rose, would you say?

parts.words: Latin-derived name for a rose, would you say?
parts.note: the flower is a red herring: rose is the past of rise, and a word from Latin circum (around) plus navigator names one who goes all the way around the world

explanation.surface: A gardener asks for the botanical Latin name of a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor who voyages right round the globe is given a Latin-built title meaning one who sails around.

clue.text: Confidential statements of party in Anglo-Saxon?

indicators.note: in says the word for party sits inside the abbreviation for Anglo-Saxon

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the private remarks were made at a party in Saxon times.
explanation.definitionFit: In a play, remarks whispered to the audience out of other characters' hearing are private comments.

clue.text: Go into field event with shaky start

parts.note: the discus is an athletics throwing event held on the field

indicators.note: the start of the word shaky is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An athlete takes up the discus throw but begins nervously.
explanation.definitionFit: To go into a topic is to examine or debate it at length, a synonym.

clue.text: Where doctors may work into the mind?

explanation.surface: Doctors on hospital rounds probe the patient's thoughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors work on hospital wards, read as two words; the single word means directed towards the inner self, the mind.

clue.text: Hack composer drops in

indicators.note: drops says the little word in is let fall from the composer's name

parts.note: Chopin was the Polish Romantic composer

explanation.surface: A hack composer pops in for a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack at something is to cut it with rough blows, a synonym.

clue.text: Shaw's captain has money tied up

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
something tied up is bound

explanation.surface: A captain in a Shaw play has his cash locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Brassbound's Conversion is a play by George Bernard Shaw; its title character is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea captain who gives his name to a George Bernard Shaw comedy, an example of a stage character.

clue.text: Index directed at foreign ref in play?

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters are moved around freely into another order

explanation.surface: A finger is pointed at a referee from abroad during the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The index finger is the pointing digit; 'directed at' is a link but also fits the surface of pointing.
explanation.definitionFit: The index is the digit next to the thumb, an anatomical synonym.

clue.text: Painter into turning over an allotment

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter

indicators.note: turning over says the letters of into are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist starts turning over the soil of his allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' suggests digging the allotment, but it is the anagram signal for INTO, giving TION; 'an allotment' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed share or portion handed out, so an allowance or allotment.

clue.text: Materials for books in Morocco, possibly

definitions.text: Materials for books in Morocco, possibly

parts.words: Materials for books in Morocco, possibly
parts.note: covers for volumes, perhaps made of morocco, the fine goatskin leather used by bookmakers, not the North African country

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where book-making supplies come from in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Book covers are often made of morocco leather, so the materials wrapping a volume are its covers.

clue.text: Oily fish fellows ate with entree starters

parts.note: fellows are men
to have had food is to have eaten it

indicators.note: starters takes only the opening pair of letters of entree, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: Some men ate an oily fish as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' keeps just EN, the first two letters of ENTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American herring relative, used for fish oil and fertiliser, an example of an oily species.

clue.text: Tailless young sheep safe here in Wales?

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter of the word for a young sheep is cut off

parts.note: a young sheep is a lamb
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A lamb whose tail has been docked is kept safe somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMPETER is a small university town in west Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a market town in Ceredigion, an example of a place in Wales.

clue.text: Envoy for beneficiary who is a bit short

indicators.note: a bit short means one letter is clipped off the end of the word for a beneficiary

parts.note: a legatee is someone left something in a will

explanation.surface: An envoy collects his inheritance, only to find it comes up short.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal ambassador or diplomatic deputy carries this title, a synonym.

clue.text: Rogues in a pack

explanation.surface: Scoundrels roam about in gangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogues are scoundrels; in a pack of cards the jacks are also called by this older name.

clue.text: Most of county on a lake that is dreamlike

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the county's name is dropped

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Most of an English county sits beside a lake that seems unreal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre and unreal like a dream, as in the art movement of Dali.

clue.text: Groups of a green disposition

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters are laid out differently

explanation.surface: Collections of people with an envious temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology these are classes of related species, ranked above species, so taxonomic categories.

clue.text: Top drawer, his aim?

parts.note: top drawer reads as the best at drawing a pistol, whose aim is literal, not a sense of high social class

explanation.surface: A socially superior person states his ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wild West duellist is the fastest at drawing his revolver and must aim true.

clue.text: Seaweed extract from Malaga rocks

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seaweed is gathered from the rocks along the Spanish coast at Malaga.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a jelly obtained from red algae, so a product of marine plants.

clue.text: Worn out piece of palimpsest

indicators.note: piece of says a short stretch of letters is taken from inside the next word

explanation.surface: A scrap of old reused parchment has become tattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted or drooping, lacking firmness, a synonym for tired.

clue.text: Tenor fitted with hairpiece, it is commonly understood

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
someone fitted with a hairpiece has been wigged

explanation.surface: A tenor in a toupee is a fact everyone knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks the definition as colloquial: to twig is informal British for to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to twig a point is to catch on to it, so grasped.

clue.text: Apostolic letter (it peels if mishandled)

indicators.note: something mishandled is treated roughly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An old letter from an apostle peels apart if it is handled carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament letters of Paul and other apostles bear this title, an example of formal writing.

clue.text: Agrippa, we learn, comes out in togas and the like

indicators.note: comes out suggests the letters emerge in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A Roman general's name, we discover, crops up in talk of togas.
explanation.definitionFit: Togas are an example of clothing, the dated phrase for garments generally.
